verdictStatement: Both turn-1 findings are repaired, and I verified each against live bytes rather than against my own turn-1 account of them. Item 2 now names DR-122's actual status cell, PROPOSED-CLOSED-FOR-REVIEW, and cites where it comes from; 'leftover-design' is gone and the bare word OPEN occurs zero times anywhere in the draft, so the clause carried over from D-114 about DR-101 is fully removed rather than patched. The Alternatives bullet was brought into line so the two sections cannot drift. DR-115 is out of the not-SATISFY list and the draft adds a sentence explaining the absence, which is both of the fixes I offered rather than one. Everything else holds. All five measured inputs and both turn-1 review digests match live; the frozen turn-1 draft is untouched at 0444 and correctly declared not retargeted; the draft's account of turn 1 is exact on both lanes, including that Codex's CONSENT 0/0 drops nothing because Codex raised no advisories; both v15 advisories survive the item-5 rewrite; the complete diff is six hunks with every one accounted for and no silent substantive change; the fifteen remaining named rows all exist; and the token audit is clean. I also tested whether the action class is legitimate at all, since DR-122 is not a plain OPEN row: adopted D-107 records a candidate against the only other PROPOSED-CLOSED-FOR-REVIEW row, so the precedent exists. My single advisory runs in the draft's favour — its wording is more precise than D-107's adopted '/ OPEN' compound, and the hygiene question belongs to that entry, not this one.

coordinatorNote: CONSENT at turn 2 on my lane. I raised the only turn-1 MUST-FIX, so I want the basis for reversing to be legible: I re-read the DR-122 status cell from live file 08 rather than trusting the repair claim, confirmed the corrected token matches it exactly, and confirmed the offending phrase is gone from the whole document rather than from the one sentence I quoted. I also walked the complete turn-1 to turn-2 diff so that a repair of two items could not carry a third change unannounced; it does not. Three things for the record. First, the draft's account of turn 1 is exact on both lanes, which I checked against the frozen files — Codex consented at 0/0 with no advisories, so nothing is lost in that shorthand, and my own OBJECT is reported with both finding ids. Second, I tested the action class rather than assuming it: DR-122 is not a plain OPEN row, and adopted D-107 establishes that a candidate may be recorded against a PROPOSED-CLOSED-FOR-REVIEW row without closing or changing it. Third, my one advisory is not a criticism of this draft and needs no change to it — this draft states the status cell exactly, while adopted D-107 writes 'PROPOSED-CLOSED-FOR-REVIEW / OPEN' for the same token even though the register counts those two states apart. If the coordinator wants the corpus to read consistently, the correction belongs to D-107 in its own cycle; amending this draft to match would make it less accurate, and I would object to that. Nothing in this verdict marks any DR SATISFIED, authorizes implementation, or mints a D-096 (A) grant, and I edited neither file 08 nor COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md.
